10 m · SENTINEL-21 m GSD · SUPER-RESOLVED

Spatial structure becomes easier to inspect.

Imagery shown in this prototype is derived from real Sentinel-2 data and super-resolution outputs used by the team; visuals are not illustrative mockups.
1 m refers to output GSD, not native satellite observation.

The scale of the transformation

10 mNative Sentinel-2 GSD
1 mTarget output GSD
100×Finer output grid density
10 m × 10 m = 100 m²

A 10 m × 10 m pixel covers 100 m². At 1 m GSD, that same area corresponds to 100 one-metre grid cells. This describes output grid density—not 100× additional observed information.

Sharper ≠ more accurate.

Super-resolution reconstructs information that was not directly observed at the target scale. We therefore evaluate the output rather than treating every reconstructed detail as ground truth.

PSNR · SSIM
